This is a site/topic hub page, not a single-area page: titled "Communities | Fraser Valley & Lower Mainland Neighbourhood Guide," it opens with a four-factor decision framework — commute, schools and catchments, price, and lifestyle — and then presents seven community blocks, with no listing feed, no market statistics table and no FAQ section in the text read.
Streets, schools and getting around Communities

items.t: The page's stated decision framework, in its own order: commute first (how often the drive will actually be done); schools, because "catchments are tighter than buyers expect" and the page advises checking actual catchment maps rather than reputation; price, because going further east buys more square footage but changes commute, community and resale dynamics; and lifestyle as the tiebreaker.
What the page does not contain: no Mission block at all, no Surrey sub-area block and no Vancouver block, and no community-by-community links list beyond the in-text links above.

Neighbourhood names named in the page's prose (inventory only, no facts imported): Walnut Grove and Willoughby Heights (Langley); Cloverdale, South Surrey, Newton and Guildford (Surrey); Ladner, Tsawwassen and North Delta (Delta).

items.t: The regulator frame behind advice taken from this page: in BC a licensed real estate professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, and only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction.

items.t: Mission is missing from a page about communities — and the homepage proves it belongs.

The page carries no statistics at all — not even for the communities SnapStats does cover. There is no market statistics table, median, sales count or ratio anywhere in the text read, so any community comparison a buyer makes from this page alone is prose against prose; the numbers live on the linked area pages.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Communities

items.t: The page ground: a hub/guide page titled "Communities | Fraser Valley & Lower Mainland Neighbourhood Guide" — not an area page for any single place and not a listing feed. It opens with a four-factor decision framework — commute, schools and catchments, price, and lifestyle — and then presents seven community blocks: Langley; Surrey / Cloverdale; White Rock / South Surrey; Abbotsford; Chilliwack; Maple Ridge / Pitt Meadows; and Delta / Ladner / Tsawwassen. Its stated position: "There's no objectively 'best' community — there's only the best fit for you."
The page contains no listing feed, no market statistics table and no FAQ section in the text read, and no Mission, Surrey sub-area or Vancouver block — Mission is not given a block at all.

Market numbers: deliberately number-free for this hub. The hub spans communities across multiple SnapStats communities and two boards; SnapStats covers exactly 14 communities with Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined splits and community-level medians only, some of the hub's ground (Chilliwack, South Delta) has no SnapStats coverage at all, and land has NO SnapStats category in any case — so no single market figure is stated for this page and none is imported from any community's row: a hub figure is not verified / not applicable.

Practice identity as the page states it: Jared Gibbons, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, Suite 201 - 15272 Croydon Dr, Surrey, BC V3Z 0Z5; office and cell 604-928-1361; email jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca; "REALTOR® since 2015" — the phone and email match Jared's confirmed public contacts.
How people search for it: "best communities Fraser Valley," "Langley vs Abbotsford living," "where to live South Surrey Langley," "Fraser Valley neighbourhood guide."

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Communities

items.t: ALR block (ALR ground exists in several hub communities; parcel status not confirmed per parcel): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

: Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

PTT — worked example (inputs + tier math; provincial, applies in every hub community): on a $500,000 lot purchase — 1% on the first $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% on $200,000–$500,000 ($6,000) = $8,000. Tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000.

blocks.text: Good to know about Communities

items.t: The hub's comparative claims are one realtor's framing, recorded as page statements only.

Coverage gaps are visible in the inventory itself (dated page read, Nov 1, 2026). Mission has no block; Chilliwack and Delta / Ladner / Tsawwassen have blocks but no onward link; Cloverdale has no block of its own (it is folded into the Surrey block); North Delta has no separate block; and no block exists for any community east of Chilliwack or in Metro Vancouver proper.

Settle the commute honestly first (a daily downtown drive changes which communities are realistic; hybrid or remote work "opens up the map"), then check the catchment map rather than reputation, then price — going further east buys more square footage but changes commute, community and resale dynamics — with lifestyle as the tiebreaker.

faq.q: Does the page say which community is best for buying a condo?
faq.a: No — its stated position is that there is no objectively "best" community, only the best fit, decided by commute, schools, price and lifestyle, and it invites the reader to talk the differences through with Jared; it names no condo building or condo stock for any community.

faq.q: Which of the page's communities link onward to fuller pages?
faq.a: Five blocks carry links in the text read — Langley (plus Willoughby Heights in its text), Surrey / Cloverdale (plus Cloverdale and South Surrey in its text), White Rock / South Surrey (plus White Rock in its text), Abbotsford, and Maple Ridge — while the Chilliwack and Delta / Ladner / Tsawwassen blocks carry no link; use the site search or the homepage's Search by Area section for those communities.

faq.q: If I pick a community here, how do I check a specific condo building?
faq.a: Through the building's own documents: the Form B Information Certificate (Strata Property Act s. 59, within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page) carries the fees, CRF balance, insurance summary and the most recent depreciation report — community prose is not a substitute.

faq.q: Can a strata in any of these communities ban me from renting out a condo I buy?
faq.a: No for long-term rentals — rental-restriction bylaws have been void province-wide since November 24, 2022; short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw, and pet and age rules remain building-specific bylaws to read on the Form B.

faq.q: Does the page say which community is best for buying land?
faq.a: No — its stated position is that there is no objectively "best" community, only the best fit, decided by commute, schools, price and lifestyle. It gives no land-specific ranking, and none is stated here.

faq.q: Are the prices quoted on the page current land or market figures?
faq.a: Price a real search from the linked area pages and current listings.

faq.q: Which bylaw governs subdividing a lot in one of these communities?
faq.a: The specific city's own bylaws — there is no hub answer.

faq.q: How much PTT on a $500,000 lot in any of these communities?
faq.a: $8,000 — 1% on the first $200,000 ($2,000) plus 2% on the next $300,000 ($6,000). PTT is provincial, so the tiers are the same in every hub community.

faq.q: Which communities does this page cover?
faq.a: Seven blocks: Langley; Surrey / Cloverdale; White Rock / South Surrey; Abbotsford; Chilliwack; Maple Ridge / Pitt Meadows; and Delta / Ladner / Tsawwassen — introduced by a decision framework covering commute, schools and catchments, price, and lifestyle.

faq.q: Does the page say which community is best?
faq.a: No — its stated position is that there is no objectively "best" community, only the best fit, decided by commute, schools, price and lifestyle, and it invites the reader to talk the differences through with Jared.

faq.q: Does the page tell me which school my child would attend in each community?
faq.a: No — the page advises checking actual catchment maps because catchments are tighter than buyers expect and one block can change the school, but it states no catchment result for any address, and none is stated in this file.
